technocore.head_message:
docs: stop counting the documents that negotiate markdown (#867)

## What

Four comments counted how many documents negotiate `text/markdown`. None
of them counts now — the code already enumerates the set, and the prose
defers to it. Comments and one test docstring only; no behaviour
changes.

## Why

The set has grown twice, and the prose did not keep up:

- `app._markdown_wanted` says **three** documents. `markdown=True`
reaches **four** paths: `_DOCS` covers `/skill.md`, `/patterns.md` and
`/interop.md`, and `auth_md` passes it too. Verified on a booted service
— all four answer `text/markdown` under `Accept: text/markdown` and
carry `Vary: Accept, Accept-Encoding`, while `/` and `/llms.txt` stay
`text/plain`.
- `manifest._prose` says **three** for the same reason.
- `test_only_the_markdown_documents_negotiate_markdown`'s docstring
enumerated `/auth.md`, `/skill.md` and `/patterns.md` while the loop
directly beneath it asserts four, `/interop.md` included. The loop is
the list; the prose was a second, staler copy.
- `app.py`'s "unlike the four `.md` files" and `manifest.py`'s "the four
URL write lanes" are both correct today (four
`{text:path}`/`{value:path}` routes), and both the same shape of claim —
the first was "three" before `/auth.md` existed.

This follows the same reasoning as the edge-lane prose in 0.14.0 (#866):
every stale claim in that area was a count that was right when written
and wrong the moment the set moved, and two of the corrected numbers on
offer across open PRs were wrong again. A number in prose is a second
copy of something the code owns, and it is the copy nobody re-derives.

This is **#354's item 5**, taken as a deletion rather than the "three →
four" correction that PR proposes, so that hunk becomes a no-op on its
rebase.

## Deliberately left to #354

- The `/humans` `Link`-header trio counts in `app.py` and `manifest.py`
— its **item 4** rewrites those exact lines, and it is a claim
correction (`/.well-known/api-catalog` is not an anchor in the page)
rather than a count. Touching them here would cost that author a
conflict on the one passage they are changing.
- Its **51 GiB → 50 GiB** arithmetic and the `agent.json` `e-` class
string: corrections, not counts.

Two more counts in `manifest.py` look **stale rather than merely
fragile** to me — the "four small documents" in the discovery-documents
section, and "three reserved namespaces" on the note lanes where the
README says four hold one note per room. I did not verify either, so
they want checking and correcting rather than a silent reword; not
touched here.

## Release note

> Comments only: the places that said how many documents negotiate
`text/markdown` now name the set instead of counting it. One of them
said three where four negotiate.

## Checks

- [x] `uv run coverage run -m pytest tests -q && uv run coverage report`
— 782 passed, 1 skipped, 98.01%
- [x] `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` and `uv run
ty check` — clean
- [x] `uv run sz.py --check` — core code-lines unchanged at 2322, so
`sz-baseline.json` stays exactly as the release left it. Neither it nor
`CHANGELOG.md` is in the diff
- [x] Docs that would now be wrong are updated: this change *is* the doc
fix; the manual and `/skill.md` need nothing
- [x] New surface on a world-writable service: **nothing new** — no
route, parameter, response or persistent state moves

sonnet.head_message:
Results: sonnet-2 — the winner, every allocation and DID, and how to check them (#86)

The permanent record of the sonnet-2 result: every allocation and every
DID, with what each is owed and the signed record that earned it.

- **Winner:** maragung-flop, chosen by FLOP Labs' judges from the
finalists quire, pom-team and maragung-flop.
- **Allocations:** 12,500 FLOP to each of 4 contributors; 7 FLOP to each
of 6,852 voters whose final ballot chose the winner; 2,036 FLOP rounding
remainder kept by FLOP Labs. 6,856 DIDs, 97,964 FLOP.
- **Verifiable:** `payouts.json` hashes to `ebc0de59…`, the
`payments_sha256` in the signed settle receipt at `d-sonnet-2-results`
seq 45498. `allocations.csv` and `payouts.json` agree DID for DID; every
file's hash is in `manifest.json`.

Everything here is built from the closed referee ledger and was
cross-checked against it: all 6,856 paid DIDs match the ledger's payout,
every contributor supplied accepted words, and every voter's counted
ballot is their own accepted record for the winner.

Adds `results/sonnet-2/` only. The pinned package and its
`manifest.json` are untouched; the package tests pass.
